title: figbank figure spec
description: A figure, made machine-readable: the one sentence it must convey, the regions and symbols it shows, the arrows between them, the status tags, the word budget for running text, and the rule by which a blind cold reader's report accepts it. The renderer (figbank/lib/figure.js) draws exactly this and nothing else; the pipeline (bin/figpipe) checks the rendering against `acceptance`.

message.description: the one sentence a cold reader must be able to recover from the picture alone (the brief's message)

brief.description: path of the human brief this spec instantiates, relative to the caller's repository

canvas.description: the viewBox in authored px; the delivery surface is named in acceptance.legibility

palette.description: named colours overriding figbank/lib/palette.js LIGHT; region/arrow `color` may name a key

word_budget.description: maximum words of running text: title + notes + arrow labels + legend; symbols, names and region titles are labels and do not count

must_not_contain.description: strings that must not appear in any text of the rendering (from the brief's must-not-contain)

frame.description: a dashed outer frame (MetaProof's meta layer) with an optional chip row inside it

tree.description: a tree laid out by figbank/lib/treelayout.js from nothing but parent pointers — positions are computed, never authored, same rule as `boundaries`. A figure has `regions` or `tree` or both; a tree this size does not fit hand-placed boxes.

parent.description: an id not present in `nodes`, or null/absent, makes this a root

label.description: short — this is a node box, not a region; wraps to at most 2 lines before it overflows

sublabel.description: one short line under the label, muted (e.g. a count, a short status word)

status.description: not constrained to the shared five-value model-variable vocabulary (#/$defs/status) — a tree's own data may have its own status words (e.g. the frontier ledger's sealed/in-progress/planned/hypothesis/killed). figbank/lib/palette.js statusStyle() recognises both sets by name; an unrecognised word gets the same neutral hollow-dot fallback as an unset status, which is a real answer ("this bank doesn't know what this status weighs"), not a schema error.

orientation.description: vertical: depth grows downward, siblings side by side (a shallow-but-wide tree). horizontal: depth grows rightward, siblings stacked top to bottom (a deep-but-narrow one, or any tree with many siblings at one level — a directory tree, almost always).

sequence.description: a sequence diagram: participants as columns, a lifeline down from each, messages as horizontal arrows in time order (figbank/lib/sequencelayout.js — column x and message y are computed from the data, never hand-placed, same rule as `tree`/`boundaries`). No activation bars in this first version (drunken-emu #14): add them only if a real instance needs them. A message may not go from a participant to itself yet — the layout function refuses it loudly rather than drawing something wrong.

label.description: short — this is a header box, not a region; wraps to at most 2 lines before it overflows

min_w.description: minimum participant header width; the actual width is computed from the label

plot.description: a statistical plot: one pair of axes (linear or log), curve series (a polyline through sampled x/y arrays) and scatter series (points, each optionally carrying an id that becomes its data-id). Ticks and the plot area are computed from the data's own range (figbank/lib/plotlayout.js), never hand-placed; mismatched array lengths, empty data, non-finite values, a non-positive value on a log axis, data outside a declared domain, and a legend that would cover data are refused loudly, never clamped or dropped (drunken-emu #23). Deliberately small: no secondary axis, bars, error bars or subplots.

box.description: the outer box, axes and labels included; the inner plot area is what is left after the tick labels are measured

y.description: same length as x (checked by the renderer, which names the series)

ids.description: scatter only: one unique id per point, rendered as that point's data-id (a React page can make it clickable)

label.description: legend entry; a series without one is not in the legend (e.g. a reference line)

end_label.description: a direct label just right of the series' right-most point, in a margin the plot reserves; two end labels closer than a text line are an error

dots.description: curve only: mark each sampled point

legend_position.description: auto: the corner with no data beneath it, else outside on the right (the plot narrows). A named corner that covers data is an error, not silently moved.

lifecycle.description: a lifecycle/state diagram: named states, transitions that may point anywhere (forward, backward, within a stage) unlike a tree's parent pointers. A state names its stage (`col`, 0-based — not a raw pixel x) and, optionally, its slot within that stage (`row`); figbank/lib/lifecyclelayout.js computes x/y from those, never from hand-authored coordinates. A transition may not connect a state to itself yet — refused loudly rather than drawn wrong (drunken-emu #15).

label.description: short — this is a state box, not a region; wraps to at most 2 lines before it overflows

col.description: which stage this state belongs to, left to right — not a pixel coordinate

row.description: slot within its stage, top to bottom; states without one keep the array's order

status.description: not constrained to the shared five-value vocabulary — figbank/lib/palette.js statusStyle() resolves any caller's own words

terminal.description: draws a second, inset border (double-border convention) — a different axis from status: can time leave this state, not what weight it carries

guard.description: a condition, rendered after the label in brackets — kept as plain text, not a separate layout element, in this first version

boundaries.description: a labelled group frame computed around a named set of regions/functionals (their own boxes, by id, plus `pad`) — the process-diagram grouping Archify calls a boundary (tt-a1i/archify): 'these four are mechanical, this one is judgment', not a data-model side. Drawn behind the regions it wraps, so it reads as a frame with a visible gap, not an overlap.

wraps.description: ids of regions/functionals already placed in `regions`; the boundary's box is their bounding box plus `pad`, never authored by hand

layout.description: region body: symbol+name list in columns, a chip flow, or nothing

grain.description: functional only: the grain it prices at; optional

formula.description: functional only: one formula line, monospace; optional

note.description: functional only: one short running-text line (counts toward the budget)

font.description: list/chips: symbols in monospace (default) or, for name-only items, the sans face

pad_top.description: extra space between the title and the body, e.g. to let a channel arrow pass through the box

terms.description: functional only: short lines under the formula (each counts toward the budget)

dotted.description: dotted line with round caps; wins over `dashed` if both are set. Two line styles let one figure carry three statuses (solid / dashed / dotted) without colour.

status.description: same rule as tree.nodes[].status: not constrained to the shared five-value vocabulary — a legend for a tree with its own status words names them here directly.

acceptance.description: the mechanical form of the brief's acceptance rule: the cold reader's claim+structure must contain the message (as keyword groups), its unreadable list must be empty, and the rendering must pass the legibility audit at the named surface

must_mention.description: groups of alternatives; every group must have at least one member present (case-insensitive substring) in the reader's claim + structure

must_not_mention.description: a reading that contains one of these has misread the figure (e.g. 'competing' for a nested stack)

width.description: delivery viewport in px for checks/svg_legibility.py

surface.description: prose: what the width and floor stand for (e.g. 'textwidth 6.5 in, 4.5 pt floor')

rounds_max.description: a brief that needs more than this many rounds is a bad brief (MetaProof #51)

label.description: required: an unlabelled axis says nothing. Counts toward word_budget.

domain.description: optional [min, max]; omitted, the domain is the data's own extent widened to the nearest tick. Data outside a declared domain is an error, not clipped.

ticks.description: target tick count for a linear axis (default 5); the actual ticks are 1-2-5 multiples

symbol.description: what is drawn (a short display form, never a truncation)

ids.description: when one drawn item stands for several model variables: their ids (id is the first)
